scope: Proposition 7.1 (Direct birth bounds) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the retained centres of one type and colour, the good masks, and the birth prescriptions of Sections 3 and 4, with the hierarchy fixed in Section 3.5. Let the finite block have mass W ≤ 1. For every fixed C > 0, the sum over all direct pairs of rmin ZZ |x−y|≤Crmax dλi(x) dλj(y) is O(1). The same-width, one-law sum X (i,j) direct ri=rj=r r X a|PI πPI (a) ZZ |x−y|≤Cre−EgX0 dνi,a(x) dνj,a(y) is O(W) + Ok0 (W1+c) for some fixed c > 0. Each ordered centre pair is counted once, at its common birth. Constants may depend on the fixed hierarchy, cutoffs, and distance constant, but not on the finite block or the slot cap N0. The additional discard used here is a static rule on medium groups, determined by their good assigned-row lists before any running-table deletions. Given any fixed δ > 0, its total first-mass loss is at most δW after choosing the fixed threshold λ0 sufficiently large. It uses only squarefree low numerator moduli. The comparison bounds remain valid after any further nonincreasing thinning of birth weights.
